searchText: I agree that aggregating ILs is not straightforward. You can't have validators to sign a shared data in one round when there are multiple IL proposers. If we aggregate ILs in append-only way rather than map-reduce fashion, it would increase complexity and require more data size. This is just an idea but what if: 1) a block proposer in slot N aggregate ILs and pass it to IL committee in slot N + 1 2) IL committee in slot N + 1 signs the IL_agg and a block proposer in slot N + 1 aggregates signatures 3) a builder in slot N + 1 is constrained by the IL_agg Not aggregating IL could be an option, but is there a slashing or penalty mechanism for IL committee? How do we know if an attester didn't receive enough ILs to validate a payload or pretend they didn't? Also, even if we go without reward for the time being, I think the design should be forward compatible. CR-related protocol services are not (strictly) part of finality, so yeah, I believe penalties (if there will ever be rewards), will apply. But not slashing IMO. >Also, even if we go without reward for the time being, I think the design should be forward compatible. 👆 I agree, even if no rewards apply in Option 1 (altruistic participation) I think this sounds nice! I also need to think more about the invalidation part but apart from that I like that the IL aggregate doesn't even have to be released over P2P What exactly does this achieve? How do we know if an attester didn't receive enough ILs to validate a payload or pretend they didn't? > We're relying on the honest majority assumption for attesters here, which I think is completely fine You can have IL committee sign the same data, which is a list of summary, so that it can be aggregated by it. This would be the expected outcome: aggregation_bits: BitVec[IL_COMMITTEE_SIZE] inclusion_summaries: List[Summary, MAX_TX_PER_IL] signature: BLSSignature It's to mitigate the issue that we can't aggregate signatures if they're signed on different data. In case we want to put something onchain for reward or what not. wrote a post on focil design resource considerations: https://ethresear.ch/t/focil-resource-design-considerations/20457

excerpts.author: jih2nn
excerpts.content:
I agree that aggregating ILs is not straightforward. You can't have validators to sign a shared data in one round when there are multiple IL proposers. If we aggregate ILs in append-only way rather than map-reduce fashion, it would increase complexity and require more data size.

This is just an idea but what if:
1) a block proposer in slot N aggregate ILs and pass it to IL committee in slot N + 1
2) IL committee in slot N + 1 signs the IL_agg and a block proposer in slot N + 1 aggregates signatures
3) a builder in slot N + 1 is constrained by the IL_agg

excerpts.author: jih2nn
excerpts.content:
Not aggregating IL could be an option, but is there a slashing or penalty mechanism for IL committee? How do we know if an attester didn't receive enough ILs to validate a payload or pretend they didn't?

Also, even if we go without reward for the time being, I think the design should be forward compatible.

excerpts.author: kboom_ro
excerpts.content:
CR-related protocol services are not (strictly) part of finality, so yeah, I believe penalties (if there will ever be rewards), will apply. But not slashing IMO. 

>Also, even if we go without reward for the time being, I think the design should be forward compatible.
👆 I agree, even if no rewards apply in Option 1 (altruistic participation)

excerpts.content: I think this sounds nice! I also need to think more about the invalidation part but apart from that I like that the IL aggregate doesn't even have to be released over P2P

excerpts.author: soispoke
excerpts.content:
How do we know if an attester didn't receive enough ILs to validate a payload or pretend they didn't?

> We're relying on the honest majority assumption for attesters here, which I think is completely fine

excerpts.author: jih2nn
excerpts.content:
You can have IL committee sign the same data, which is a list of summary, so that it can be aggregated by it. This would be the expected outcome:

aggregation_bits: BitVec[IL_COMMITTEE_SIZE]
inclusion_summaries: List[Summary, MAX_TX_PER_IL]
signature: BLSSignature

excerpts.author: jih2nn
excerpts.content: It's to mitigate the issue that we can't aggregate signatures if they're signed on different data. In case we want to put something onchain for reward or what not.
